decision: One exact synthetic P249 ACES2065-1/AP0/D60 OpenEXR is mechanically interoperable with the already-installed OpenImageIO 3.1.11.0 Windows runtime. Retain this as private third-party reader compatibility only; do not add a dependency or broaden the P249/P251 claim.
preformal_exclusions: The first focused invocation compared identity dictionaries including path labels; the comparison was narrowed to identity keys before any OpenImageIO read.

The first OpenImageIO read passed, but the parent process retained the temporary OpenEXR native module and blocked Windows cleanup. P249 reconstruction was moved to a child process before formal lock; source, container, pixels, metadata and gates did not change.

One owned preformal prototype directory and one failed-cleanup directory under outputs/tmp remain quarantined because the execution policy rejected recursive deletion. They are outside formal runs and are not counted as formal residue.
claim_ceiling: Private interoperability of one exact synthetic P249 AP0/D60 ACES2065-1 OpenEXR with one existing Windows OpenImageIO runtime only; no arbitrary EXR/ACES, image quality, SMPTE certification, public dependency/API/package/schema/capability, renderer/product mapping or candidate-3 change.
